title: Need Guidance: Starting Algo Trading from Scratch
author: No-Interest-631
selftext:
Hello everyone!

I've been doing manual trading for quite some time, but I'm a complete beginner in Algo Trading, coding and bot development.

I want to learn how to build my own Python-based Algo Trading system for Indian markets, mainly NIFTY / BANKNIFTY Options.

I'd appreciate some guidance on a few things:

1. How should I start learning Algo Trading from scratch?

2. Which AI is best for developing a trading bot — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or something else?

3. Which broker would you recommend for Python-based Algo Trading?

4. How much historical data and how many months of backtesting are sufficient before going live?

5. What tools, platforms or Python libraries should I learn?

6. Any expert advice, learning resources or mistakes I should avoid as a beginner?

My Initial Plan:

\- Total capital: ₹20,000

\- Active trading capital: ₹10,000–₹15,000

\- Proposed daily maximum loss: ₹500

\- Trading style: Intraday Options Buying

\- Initial goal: Signal generation only (manual execution)

\- Approach: Backtesting → Paper Trading → Live Trading

I'm not looking for shortcuts or guaranteed profits. I want to learn and build a properly tested system from scratch.

Experienced algo traders, your suggestions and practical advice would be highly appreciated! 🙏

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
start from what you already have. you've traded by hand for a while, so write your best setup down as rules exact enough that a stranger could follow them: entry, exit, stop, size, what time of day. that document is the hard part, the code is the easy part now.

which AI matters less than people think, any of the three will write the Python. what matters is that you can read what it wrote, so go slow enough to follow every line. the bugs that hurt are the quiet ones, like a rule peeking at a candle that hasn't closed yet.

on how much history: count trades, not months. a few hundred trades across a calm stretch, a trending one and at least one ugly expiry week tells you more than 'six months' does. and for NIFTY options you need actual option prices with the spread, backtesting on the index alone will flatter you.

broker, no idea, I only know the US side. someone local will know better.

comments.author: No_Car1901
comments.body: Start with FreqAI. Need changes though.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
One thing worth checking before any code: with Rs 10,000-15,000 and intraday option buying, the costs per round trip (brokerage, STT, exchange fees, plus the bid/ask spread) can eat a big part of a small target. Put them in the backtest from day one, otherwise almost every scalp looks profitable.

  
Historical intraday option data is the hard part for NIFTY/BANKNIFTY. Expiries and strikes keep changing, so you need the actual contract that was ATM at that moment, not a continuous series. A practical start is to generate signals on the index candles first and see if they have any edge there, then test on real option prices only for the signals that survive.

  
On "how many months": count trades, not months. A few hundred trades across trending and choppy days, expiry days included, tell you much more than 6 months of one regime. Also your Rs 500 daily stop is about 3-5% of trading capital, so simulate a streak of bad days before going live.

comments.author: New-Presentation3801
comments.body: For NIFTY options, reliable historical option chain data matters more than whether Claude or ChatGPT writes the Python. Your ₹500 daily loss limit should be enforced by the program itself. Moon serves a different type of directional market activity, so I'd keep your project focused on proper options backtesting and signal generation first.

comments.author: surkur
comments.body:
AI does matter. having used all 3, i wouldnt touch gemini with a 10 foot pole let alone trust it with my money. Claude is decent and then gpt. it matters what rules you set for the AI to find you the edge otherwise it will just regurgitate its own general knowledge and make u fall for seo traps.

step1: make it download all the required data  and seal a good chunk and never touch it.  so that once you have done enough backtesting and have high confidence edges, only that pool gets tested on a small chunk of sealed data. 

every edge it finds, make it start forward logs and score them weekly. 

use duckdb+parquet over sqlite for database so your work is faster and more efficient. 

tell it not to run tests with the purpose of closing tickets, instead every test is an opportunity to hunt for clues.
